config.title: useDeferredValue

intro.title: useDeferredValue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a searchable product list that demonstrates how to keep the interface responsive during user typing. You will learn the core concept of deferring a non-urgent state update to prevent the UI from freezing or lagging. The main technologies involved are the React useDeferredValue Hook and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to apply this Hook to improve performance in real-time input scenarios.
intro.usecase: The useDeferredValue hook is essential for optimizing real-time search interfaces in applications like e-commerce product filters or admin dashboards. When a user types into a search bar, it allows the UI to remain responsive by deferring the rendering of computationally expensive results—such as filtering large datasets or fetching suggestions—until after urgent updates like keystrokes are handled. This pattern prevents laggy typing experiences in complex UIs, ensuring smooth interactions in data-heavy components like live data tables, autocomplete dropdowns, or dynamic chart updates.

objectives: Implement a React component that uses the useDeferredValue hook to manage deferred state updates.
Apply useDeferredValue to a text input to defer a computationally expensive rendering operation.
Construct a UI with a controlled input and a separate display area that shows deferred results.
Configure TypeScript types for the deferred value to ensure type safety in the component.
Update the component to handle user input while maintaining responsiveness with deferred rendering.
Integrate useDeferredValue with React.memo to optimize performance by preventing unnecessary re-renders.
Manipulate the deferred value in a simulated slow-rendering list or calculation to observe its effect.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element. The component should be defined with TypeScript.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns some JSX content, like a div with a heading.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useDeferredValue } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined yet. Create a functional component named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named inputValue with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value and destructure the returned array into inputValue and setInputValue.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [name, setName] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable inputValue initialized to an empty string.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into inputValue and setInputValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty string initial value and destructuring the array into inputValue and setInputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use useState to create a state variable named inputValue with an empty string initial value.

steps.title: Apply useDeferredValue to the state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, call useDeferredValue with the inputValue state variable and assign the result to a new constant named deferredValue.
steps.hint: useDeferredValue returns a deferred version of the value you pass to it. Store it in a variable to use later.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a deferred value
const deferredInput = useDeferredValue(inputValue);
steps.expectedOutcome: A deferred version of inputValue is created and stored in a variable named deferredValue.
successCriteria: useDeferredValue is called with inputValue and the result is assigned to a constant named deferredValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling useDeferredValue with inputValue and storing the result in a variable named deferredValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use the useDeferredValue hook with inputValue and assign it to deferredValue.

steps.title: Create a handler for input changes
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named handleChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> as a parameter and updates the inputValue state with the event's target.value.
steps.hint: Define the function with the correct parameter type and call setInputValue inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleChange function is defined that updates the inputValue state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The handleChange function is defined with the correct parameter type and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but check the parameter type or the setInputValue call.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function isn't defined correctly. Make sure it takes a ChangeEvent parameter and calls setInputValue.

steps.title: Add the input element
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your component, add an input element with type='text', value bound to inputValue, and onChange wired to handleChange.
steps.hint: Remember to use the JSX syntax for the input element. The value attribute should be set to inputValue, and onChange should call handleChange.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a controlled input element
<input type="text" value={someValue} onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: A controlled input field that updates the inputValue state when the user types.
successCriteria: The input element is present with type='text', value={inputValue}, and onChange={handleChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the input has all three required attributes: type='text', value={inputValue}, and onChange={handleChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added an input with the correct attributes.

steps.title: Simulate expensive computation with deferred value
steps.instruction: Create a function named simulateExpensiveComputation that takes a string parameter and returns an array of strings. Inside the function, generate 1000 items where each item is the parameter repeated with its index (e.g., 'item-0', 'item-1').
steps.hint: Define the function with proper TypeScript typing: (value: string) => string[]. Use a for loop or Array.from to create the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named simulateExpensiveComputation is defined that generates an array of 1000 strings based on its input parameter.
successCriteria: The simulateExpensiveComputation function exists with proper TypeScript typing and returns an array of 1000 items where each item combines the input string with its index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
